correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the common-neighbor facets of each parity component, proves that every face with at least three vertices has a unique facet, and supplies an explicit descending-cardinality elementary collapse in every facet while retaining all shared faces. The collapsed \(2\)-complex has the stated face counts. Its fundamental group is killed by replacing every weight-two diagonal not using coordinate \(1\) with a two-edge generator path and observing that pairs of retained triangles fill every coordinate square of the \(d-1\)-cube. The resulting simply connected \(2\)-complex has free \(H_2\) of rank \(\mu_d\) by Euler characteristic, and Whitehead's theorem gives the wedge of \(2\)-spheres. The packaged verifier reconstructs \(4\le d\le7\) from the graph definition and independently checks matching coverage, finite acyclicity, and homology.

value.rationale: Hypercubes are a canonical infinite family, while each neighborhood facet has dimension \(d-1\). The theorem gives a uniform collapse to dimension two and an exact closed formula for the number of sphere summands, growing on the order of \(2^d d^2\). This is a structural all-parameter homotopy classification, not a routine finite computation or a restatement of the abstract homology of \(Q_d\).
